chapter: Reel 2: touring, shows and the war
title: Show failure; City Island Showboat; television hurts live music
summary: Lazy Rhythm closes, then the band plays the Showboat, as television rises.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: How the music business changed: hype, youth and lost apprenticeship

blocks.x: Can you tell me more about that show?
Oh, the James P. Johnson show had a

-- well, we had to work with a group of people in there. I don't remember them all now, but -- because I played so many shows. They had the regular setup -- showgirls and the comedians and I really don't remember who they were, I'll tell you the truth.

All I remember is that it didn't last long, and we were so upset. I got my money, and whoever told us it was going to be a long run -- yeah, one week. Didn't have the correct backing. Now, Maxine's was a different place. Very nice. And when that closed, Maxine's closed, we went to City Island, at the Showboat, it was a place in City Island that we went to.

And McGuire was the name of the boss there, McGuire. And we played there for about -- oh, two or three months, I think. Yeah. That was nice. We used to drive out there every night. Now, during that time, television was beginning to sneak in, only rich people had it at that time because -- and the big bands, one by one, was starting to wake up, and nightclubs were starting to fold up. Because during that era when television came in, everything went out, all that live music.
